mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the past 6 months indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS shows sustained growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 3 months signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) are increasing, it signals a tight labor market with wage pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to inflation concerns.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS is increasing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 6 months, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals strong economic growth and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST is increasing and UNRATE is decreasing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of economic expansion, a decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past 3 months, coupled with a rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL), signals supply chain disruptions and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: economic expansion with supply chain disruptions
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% and CPIAUCSL is rising during economic expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.
